title: Modifications to Platelet-Rich Fibrin (PRF): Utilizing the Bio-Heat Technology
html:
Written by: Drs. Richard Miron and Nathan Estrin

INTRODUCTION

Platelet concentrates have been utilized in many fields of regenerative medicine owing to their ability to deliver supraphysiological concentrations of autologous platelets, leukocytes, and growth factors.1,2 While platelet-rich plasma (PRP) has been extensively employed as a first-generation platelet concentrate, platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) has since been utilized with a better ability to release more growth factors over an extended period of time, with superior clinical outcomes in various fields of medicine and dentistry.3,4 PRF has proven to be an excellent biomaterial composed of autogenous cells and growth factors entrapped within a fibrin network that have been shown to break down more slowly over time when compared to traditional PRP.4

Nevertheless, one of the main reported drawbacks of PRF (and especially PRP) is its faster-than-ideal resorption rate characterized within a 2- to 3-week timeframe.5 Because of its fast resorption rate, PRF membranes cannot be utilized as a barrier membrane similar to collagen owing to their inability to exclude soft tissues over an extended period of time. Interestingly, a number of recent studies have demonstrated that PRF could be significantly extended from 2- to 3-week resorption properties to greater than 4 months (extended-PRF; e-PRF) by heating a liquid platelet-poor plasma (PPP) layer (denaturing albumin) using Bio-Heat technology.6

The heated version of plasma, which has now been utilized in many areas of medicine and dentistry, has recently been the basis of intensive research endeavors across many regenerative labs owing to its extended working properties. Since one of the main limitations of PRP/PRF has historically been its short in vivo turnover rate, these extended PRF membranes can be used as substitutes for collagen membranes in guided bone regeneration (GBR) procedures requiring a typical ‘barrier’ function that protects bone regeneration from faster growing soft tissues.7

To overcome the quick degradation properties of platelet concentrates and better maintain volume stability, the Alb-PRF protocol was developed. This protocol involves the use of the PPP layer (containing ~60% albumin) and heating it to 75°C for 10 minutes to allow for albumin denaturation as well as breaking of many weak linkages or bonds (eg, hydrogen bonds) within its protein molecules. Following denaturation, the proteins are then restructured in a more densely organized assembly that extends the resorption properties of PRF to up to 4 to 6 months.8-11 However, the heating process also destroys cells/growth factors, and thereby, the platelet concentrates lose much of their regeneration potential. For these reasons, a concentrated PRF layer (C-PRF)12,13 taken from the buffy coat is then mixed back into the heated PPP (albumin gel) once cooling has occurred (termed Alb-PRF or e-PRF for extended PRF).14

In view of previous research to date on this topic, the aim of this product review was to present the biological properties of this novel regenerative modality. As an injectable filler, a 25G needle or 22G cannula is recommended. Alternatively, a similar process can be utilized to create a custom shape membrane with extended properties (e-PRF) lasting up to 4 to 6 months and utilized clinically as a substitute for collagen membranes (Figure 1).

Clinical Use of Alb-PRF/e-PRF Membranes for Periodontology and Implant Dentistry

One of the main areas where the e-PRF membranes were first clinically utilized and tested was as a substitute for collagen membranes. Therefore, several clinical case series were started whereby the e-PRF membranes were created and utilized for extraction site management to cover bone allografts following tooth removal similar to either a collagen membrane/plug or a PTFE membrane. This opportunity offers the clinician a 100% all-natural biomaterial with extended resorption properties that can also be left exposed in the oral cavity following placement. Notably, the e-PRF membranes may also be left exposed in the oral cavity, and their inclusion of supra-physiological concentrations of leukocytes allows for greater defense against incoming pathogens. Several research articles by our team have demonstrated the use of e-PRF membranes used over extract sites highlighting the much much faster soft tissue closure ability of epithelial tissue when compared to alternative strategies such as PTFE or collagen membranes.15-17

E-PRF membranes have also been utilized extensively during GBR procedures (Figure 2). Here, such membranes may be much less foreign to soft tissues, with reports of improved biocompatibility. Finally, e-PRF membranes have also been utilized as a substitute for various collagen membranes during recession coverage procedures utilizing a vestibular tunneling approach (Figure 3).

Clinical Studies Using e-PRF as an Injectable Bio-Filler

To date, thousands of cases have utilized the technology of extending the working properties of platelet concentrates as a biological filler (Bio-Filler). One of the first approaches was to restore the facial volume (Figure 4). Interestingly, Alb-PRF has been utilized for injections into deficient papillae with quite promising results, yielding up to 4 years of data (Figure 5). Lastly, Alb-PRF has also been utilized as a biological growth factor for joint and spinal injections such as diseased osteoarthritic joints and spinal injections.

ABOUT THE AUTHORS

Dr. Miron is a lead educator and researcher at Advanced PRF Education and an adjunct visiting faculty in the department of Periodontology in Bern, Switzerland where he completed his PhD studies since 2009. For the past 10 years, Dr. Miron has also been recognized by Dentistry Today as a Leaders in CE. He is the #1 ranked researcher on Platelet-Rich Fibrin therapy per Expertscape independent review and developed many novel technologies and protocols including the injectable liquid-PRF formulations, optimized protocols utilizing horizontal centrifugation, and the longer lasting form of PRF termed extended-PRF through the BioHeat process. He has published over 450 peer-reviewed articles and written 10 textbooks including his best-sellers, Next Generation Biomaterials for Bone and Periodontal Regeneration, Understanding Platelet Rich Fibrin, and Modern Implant Dentistry. Dr. Miron has been awarded many international prizes including the ITI Andre Schroeder Prize, the IADR Young Investigator of the Year in the field of Implant Dentistry, as well as the IADR Socransky Research award in the field of periodontology. He can be reached at rick@themironlab.com.

Dr. Estrin is a board-certified periodontist practicing the most modern periodontal procedures and clinical research. Dr. Estrin received his bachelor’s degree in Kinesiology from Indiana University and his DMD degree at LECOM school of Dental Medicine in Florida. Dr. Estrin further specialized in periodontology at Stony Brook University, NY, where he not only enjoyed his 3-year residency program specialized in implants and periodontal regenerative therapy but also developed a passion for research and contributing to the field. Today, Dr. Estrin practices in Lakewood Ranch, Fla, combining evidence-based care with a commitment to continued innovation. Despite being a full-time clinician, he remains deeply involved in research and education, with more than 50 publications and 4 book chapters to his name. His professional interests focus on regenerative dentistry and bridging the gap between scientific research and real-world clinical application. Dr. Estrin also serves as adjunct faculty at the LECOM School of Dental Medicine and the University of Iowa and is a lead educator for PRFedu, helping dental offices implement and better understand emerging technologies and treatment advancements. He can be reached at drnathan@estrinperiodontics.com

Disclosure: Dr. Miron is the founder of Advanced PRF Education and holds intellectual property and performs live courses affiliated with Platelet Rich Fibrin Therapy. Dr. Estrin reports no disclosures.
